project.name: Brownmuir
project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Full strict-boundary audit. Brownmuir remains selector-only at 24 and does not appear on the town map. Direct checks found no qualifying See place, café/coffee-and-cake stop, named local trail, picnic site, visitor parking or public toilet within the boundary. Fordoun House is private and the medieval moat is archaeological rather than a managed visitor attraction; both remain visible, dated HES heat records. Fordoun and A90 businesses outside the boundary are not borrowed. The former airfield domestic site is retained as an NRHE record but is not presented as a visitor attraction. No dedicated Treasure Trails, Curious About, Mystery Guides or Go Quest product was found.

touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Ordinary responsible countryside access may be possible, but no destination-scale dog visit or dedicated facilities are verified.

townGuide.headline: A mapped locality rather than a visitor destination
townGuide.intro: Brownmuir remains a 24% selector-only settlement. Its statutory heritage is retained on the historic heat layer, but private heritage and nearby Fordoun services are not converted into Brownmuir visitor cards.
perfectFor: Identifying the locality while planning a wider Mearns route

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Treat it as a route reference
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: There is no verified visitor itinerary within the strict Brownmuir boundary; plan facilities and attractions elsewhere.

townGuide.visitorMood: A quiet rural locality with statutory heritage but no verified public visitor offer.

features.fullDescription: Dated 1712 at window lintel, somewhat altered. Former dower house, now farmhouse. Large 3-storey 5 window gabled block, harled with large modern glass porch. Slated roof with straight skews and big end stacks, single storey wing.
